Report_ID: Relapse by 12 months (complement of sustained remission at 1 year)
Title: Efficacy of rituximab versus tacrolimus in difficult-to-treat steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome: an open-label pilot randomized controlled trial
Author: Mathew G, Sinha A, Ahmed A, Grewal N, Khandelwal P, Hari P, Bagga A
Comment: Relapse event counts (9/20 per arm) derived as the complement of the explicitly reported sustained-remission counts (11 of 20 in each arm; also 55% relapse-free in both arms at 12 months per Fig. 3a). The paper's own reported risk ratio of 1.0 [0.57, 1.75] and risk difference 0% refer to sustained REMISSION (favourable outcome), not relapse, so they were not entered into the ratio fields; M_diff=0 is the paper's reported risk difference (0%). P=0.50 is one-sided for non-inferiority. Denominator is the modified ITT population (n=20 rituximab, 20 tacrolimus); 21 were randomized to rituximab but one never returned.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Rituximab (IV 375 mg/m2 x 2 doses one week apart)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: open-label parallel-group pilot non-inferiority randomized controlled trial
Participant type: Children aged 3-18 years with difficult-to-treat steroid-sensitive (frequently relapsing or steroid-dependent) nephrotic syndrome
Outcome measurement: Number of children not in sustained remission (i.e. experiencing >=1 relapse) at 12 months out of modified ITT population per arm
Outcome variable: Relapse by 12 months (complement of sustained remission at 1 year)

Report_ID: Relapse of nephrotic syndrome by 12 months (children with >=1 relapse)
Title: Comparison of rituximab, cyclophosphamide, and tacrolimus as first steroid-sparing agents for complicated relapsing/steroid-dependent nephrotic syndrome in children: an evaluation of the health-related quality of life
Author: Wang L, Zhu J, Xia M, Hua R, Deng F
Comment: Event counts were NOT reported verbatim; they were derived arithmetically from the explicitly reported relapse-free survival percentages and the explicit per-arm n = 17 (82.4% x 17 = 14 relapse-free -> 3 relapsed; 64.7% x 17 = 11 relapse-free -> 6 relapsed). The reported adjusted Cox HR of 2.346 is oriented as tacrolimus/cyclophosphamide risk relative to rituximab (favouring rituximab) and had p = 0.228, which conflicts with the log-rank p = 0.043 quoted in the Results text.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Rituximab (375 mg/m2 single dose, repeated at 6-month intervals)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: children with frequently relapsing/steroid-dependent nephrotic syndrome, steroid-sparing-agent naive
Recruitment source: Children's Hospital of Anhui Medical University
Outcome measurement: Number of children relapsing within 1 year, derived from reported 1-year relapse-free survival percentages (82.4% and 64.7% of n = 17 per arm)
Outcome variable: Relapse of nephrotic syndrome by 12 months (children with >=1 relapse)
additional_group_ns: Cyclophosphamide arm (not part of the planned comparison): n = 17, 1-year relapse-free survival 11.8% (i.e. 15/17 relapsed)

Report_ID: Children with relapse by 12 months (complement of 12-month relapse-free survival), ITT
Title: Efficacy of Rituximab vs Tacrolimus in Pediatric Corticosteroid-Dependent Nephrotic Syndrome: A Randomized Clinical Trial
Author: Basu et al.
Comment: Relapse event counts derived as randomized total minus patients with sustained remission (60-54=6 rituximab; 60-38=22 tacrolimus); this is corroborated by the paper's own text ("the 6 patients who subsequently developed relapses displayed higher B-cell counts than the 54 who did not relapse"). The paper reports P < .001 (recorded as 0.001, an upper bound). The paper's reported OR of 5.21 (95% CI 1.93-14.07) is for SUSTAINED REMISSION with tacrolimus as reference (i.e. favoring rituximab), so it is directionally inverse to the relapse outcome recorded here and was deliberately not entered into the odds_ratio field to avoid sign inversion in pooling. One patient with missing primary end point data was imputed with the group's most common value.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Rituximab (single course, 2 infusions of 375 mg/m2 plus 4 weeks alternate-day prednisolone)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: randomized controlled trial (open-label, parallel-arm, single-center, phase 3)
Participant type: Children aged 3-16 years with corticosteroid-dependent nephrotic syndrome, no previous corticosteroid-sparing agent exposure
Recruitment source: Consecutive children attending a single tertiary care pediatric nephrology unit (Nilratan Sircar Medical College and Hospital, Kolkata)
Outcome measurement: Number of children experiencing one or more relapses during the 12-month study period out of total randomized per arm
Outcome variable: Children with relapse by 12 months (complement of 12-month relapse-free survival), ITT
